council_meetings.headline: After a second public input session, the Council accepted and adopted the City's Housing Action Plan 8-0, and gave final approval to making Fleet Street one-way with a contraflow bike lane.

decisions.title: Accepted and adopted the Housing Action Plan
decisions.detail: Planning Director Peter Britz presented the plan's action items, zoning actions and incentives, and four residents spoke at the input session. Councilors said more work is needed, citing slow timelines, rents, parking and the lack of federal money for public housing. Councilor Tabor will bring ideas raised back to the Housing Committee.
decisions.review_note: Minutes say the motion was "Seconded by Councilor Moreau," the same councilor who made it. The actual seconder needs to be confirmed, so seconded_by is left null.

decisions.title: Gave final approval to making Fleet Street one-way with a contraflow bike lane
decisions.detail: Fleet Street will run one-way from Congress Street to Hanover Street, with a bike lane running the opposite direction.

decisions.title: Gave final approval to moving Fleet Street parking to the east side
decisions.detail: Parking spaces on Fleet Street will move from the west side to the east side.

decisions.title: Adopted zoning changes on variance procedures and when approvals expire
decisions.detail: The changes cover procedures for variances (permission to break a zoning rule for one property), special exceptions and appeals, and when land use approvals, including wetland permits, expire or can be extended.

decisions.title: Adopted new rules on board appointments, terms and removal
decisions.detail: No one spoke at the hearing on the change to Administrative Code Section 1.302 (D). The Council passed second reading, suspended its rules and passed third and final reading the same night.

decisions.title: Expanded downtown workforce parking eligibility through March 1, 2027
decisions.detail: Starting October 1, 2026, the Downtown Workforce Parking Program is open to downtown workers in clerical, customer service, administrative and support staff jobs at businesses that previously took part, until March 1, 2027. Councilors discussed hourly versus salaried workers. Councilor Hopkins abstained because a family member works downtown.

decisions.title: Asked staff for off-peak parking options for downtown businesses
decisions.detail: Staff will report back in October on parking options for downtown businesses that need off-peak parking during the workweek.

decisions.title: Directed staff to look for City land for natural burials
decisions.detail: The City Manager will dedicate staff time, or recommend money, to find out whether any City-owned land is suitable for natural burials, and recommend FY2028 capital funding to set this up on City land or through buying land.

decisions.title: Sent the Housing Authority's Sherburne sewer request to staff for review
decisions.detail: The Portsmouth Housing Authority asked for a sewer extension and reimbursement agreement for its Sherburne housing project. Legal, Finance and Public Works will review it and report back. Councilors had asked many questions about the project's financing.

decisions.title: Asked for a report back on plans with Prescott Park Arts Festival for a covered stage
decisions.detail: The report follows up on an April motion for the City to work with the Festival on park improvements, including a covered stage and related structures paid for by the Festival. Councilor Bagley also asked Legal to report on the Prescott Park trust funds and City contributions.

decisions.title: Released $9,500 from the Lower State Street Pocket Park Trust
decisions.detail: The money pays for landscape consulting and coordinating the installation of a sculpture in the pocket park.

decisions.title: Accepted a water service easement from 1151 Sagamore Avenue
decisions.detail: An easement gives the City a legal right to use part of private land, here for water service access.

decisions.title: Approved a landscaping agreement with 145 Maplewood Avenue
decisions.detail: The City Manager may negotiate and sign an agreement with 145 Maplewood Avenue, LLC for landscaping installation and maintenance.

decisions.title: Accepted a $14,868 federal justice assistance grant for the Police Department
decisions.detail: The grant comes from the Edward Byrne Memorial Justice Assistance Grant (JAG) Program.

decisions.title: Accepted more donations for the Point of Graves cemetery wall
decisions.detail: Six more individual donations were accepted for the wall replacement, in amounts listed in the donation forms.

decisions.title: Accepted a $1,000 Sister Cities donation in honor of Eileen Dondero Foley
decisions.detail: Mary Carey Foley donated $1,000 to the new Sister Cities special revenue fund.

decisions.title: Made appointments to the Public Art Review Committee, Library Board and Economic Development Commission
decisions.detail: John Bohenko joins the Public Art Review Committee and Richard Samdperil the Library Board of Trustees. Jason Goodrich moves from alternate to full member, and Thomas Watson and Anne Weidman were reappointed, on the Economic Development Commission.

decisions.title: Approved the Scarecrows of the Port event
decisions.detail: Approved on the consent agenda (routine items approved in one vote).

discussed.title: Sherburne School housing project update
discussed.detail: The Portsmouth Housing Authority and its development team updated the Council on the Sherburne project, including Phase 2, next steps and financing. Councilors asked about the amount of financing needed and infrastructure costs.

discussed.title: Stormwater utility evaluation
discussed.detail: Raftelis Financial Consultants presented on a possible stormwater utility (a separate fee to pay for managing rain runoff). Staff noted that in Boston most residents saw lower bills because sewer charges dropped more than stormwater charges rose. Councilors stressed public communication.

discussed.title: City Manager evaluation
discussed.detail: Councilor Tabor reported on the City Manager evaluation, praising her budget work, leadership and support of Council goals.

discussed.title: Other updates
discussed.detail: Household Hazardous Waste Collection Day is Saturday, October 24. The Shuttle Loop Working Group's first meeting is October 19. An updated RAPP map will be in the October 13 packet. Councilor Moreau gave a brief Planning Board update on a Heritage Commission.

public_comment.gist: Speakers raised Prescott Park, parking, housing, and burial and cemetery options.

Speakers advocated housing for all, described ways to address housing, raised costs for single-income households on fixed incomes and suggested boarding houses, and called for free public housing, citing a gap between homeowners and renters.

coming_up.item: Temporary expansion of downtown workforce parking eligibility ends

council_meetings.headline: The Council reworked the Resident Access Parking Program (RAPP) pilot, including removing part of Parrott Avenue from it on a 5-3 roll call, kept resident parking rates at $1.25 an hour, and accepted up to $240,000 to rebuild the Point of Graves cemetery wall.

decisions.title: Removed part of Parrott Avenue from the RAPP pilot
decisions.detail: The motion takes the section of Parrott Avenue from Roger Street to Richards Avenue out of the RAPP policy, as amended to allow 4 hours of free parking. Councilor Blalock cited recreation programs; Councilor Hopkins raised library and school staff parking. Several councilors said they wanted more data before changing parking on Parrott Avenue.
decisions.outcome: passed 5-3 on a roll call vote

decisions.title: Added 4 hours of free parking to the Parrott Avenue motion
decisions.detail: This amendment to the Parrott Avenue motion provides free parking for 4 hours.
decisions.review_note: Minutes record "Motion passed 7-1 (Mayor McEachern)" without saying how the Mayor voted. Councilor Tabor is recorded as opposing "this motion" during the debate, yet only one dissent is recorded. Confirm the dissenter against the video.

decisions.title: Kept resident parking rates at $1.25 an hour
decisions.detail: Residents will keep paying $1.25 an hour for the first 3 hours and $2.25 an hour after that for on-street and lot parking in FY2027.

decisions.title: Considered raising nonresident parking to $3 and $6 an hour starting October 1
decisions.detail: The motion would raise the nonresident on-street and lot rate from $2 an hour for the first 3 hours and $5 after that, to $3 and $6. Councilors Cook, Moreau, Hopkins and Tabor and Assistant Mayor Kelley spoke in favor. An amendment setting an October 1, 2026 effective date passed 8-0.
decisions.outcome: no final vote recorded (amendment for an October 1 effective date passed 8-0)
decisions.review_note: The minutes record the 8-0 vote on the effective-date amendment but no vote on the main motion as amended. Confirm whether the $3/$6 nonresident rate was adopted.

decisions.title: Adjusted the downtown workforce parking program
decisions.detail: Changes to the RAPP policy remove the 35 cent transaction fee for workforce parking on Parrott Avenue, raise Foundry Garage workforce stickers from 10 to 12 hours, raise monthly stickers from 20 to 26, and define eligible workers as small business owners and employees of downtown restaurant, hospitality, retail and personal service businesses.

decisions.title: Limited the Parrott Avenue Lot to residents and downtown workers, at no charge
decisions.detail: The RAPP policy now limits the Parrott Avenue Lot to resident and downtown workforce parking, with a few spaces set aside for Portsmouth District Court defendants. An amendment to charge no fee passed 8-0 before the final vote.

decisions.title: Accepted up to $240,000 to replace the Point of Graves cemetery wall
decisions.detail: An anonymous South End resident donated up to $240,000 for the wall replacement. In a second 8-0 vote the Council accepted additional donations from residents, families and Geno's Chowder and Sandwich Shop, raised with help from Friends of the South End.

decisions.title: Created a Shuttle Loop and Public Transit Working Group
decisions.detail: The time-limited group will pull together existing studies and data on expanding public transit and report back by January 29, 2027 with a recommended pilot or a design scope for a consultant. Councilor Blalock called it unrealistic; Councilor Tabor noted state law allows parking money to fund transit.

decisions.title: Asked for a solar generation plan, including a $4.1 million Jones Avenue array
decisions.detail: Staff will prepare a plan for solar on City land and buildings, including smaller high-return projects and a solar array at the Jones Avenue landfill listed as a $4.1 million item in the Capital Improvement Plan. Report back is due October 13.

decisions.title: Passed first reading on moving most parking rules from zoning into site plan review
decisions.detail: Parking requirements for most projects (not one- and two-family homes) would move from the Zoning Ordinance to the Planning Board's Site Plan Review Regulations. Two amendments passed 8-0: striking "and loading zones" from Section 10.232.38 and striking Section 10.244.50 on conditional use permit conditions. Public hearing and second reading are set for October 13.

decisions.title: Passed first reading of a Historic District boundary change
decisions.detail: The zoning map change adds and removes parcels from the Historic District. Councilor Cook said it brings the map in line with the Middle Street District by removing properties not on Middle Street. Public hearing and second reading are set for October 13.

decisions.title: Passed second reading of zoning changes on variance notices and when approvals expire
decisions.detail: The changes cover procedures for variances (permission to break a zoning rule for one property), special exceptions and appeals, and the expiration of approvals including wetland conditional use permits. Councilors asked how neighbors are notified; currently direct abutters are. No one spoke at the hearing. Third reading is set for September 28.

decisions.title: Passed second reading to move Fleet Street parking to the east side
decisions.detail: Staff explained the contraflow bike lane, sidewalks and ADA access, with construction possibly in late fall and early spring. Three people spoke at the hearing. Third reading is set for September 28.

decisions.title: Passed second reading to make Fleet Street one-way with a contraflow bike lane
decisions.detail: Fleet Street would run one-way from Congress Street to Hanover Street, with a bike lane going the opposite direction. No one spoke at the hearing. Third reading is set for September 28.

decisions.title: Passed first reading on rules for board appointments, terms and removal
decisions.detail: The change to Administrative Code Section 1.302 (D) goes to a public hearing and second reading on September 28.

decisions.title: Approved an agreement with school paraeducators
decisions.detail: The Council accepted the Memorandum of Agreement for Portsmouth School District paraeducators (classroom aides).

decisions.title: Approved the employment agreement for Deputy Fire Chief Scott Egan
decisions.detail: The Council accepted the proposed agreement as presented.

decisions.title: Asked for a status update on the Sherburne School project
decisions.detail: City staff, with the Portsmouth Housing Authority, will update the Council on progress, timelines, milestones and challenges for the project.

decisions.title: Asked for a report on the former recreation area under the I-95 bridge
decisions.detail: Councilors want to see if the space can better serve the Atlantic Heights community, possibly with public art.

decisions.title: Sent a petition to discontinue part of Cornwall Street to the Planning Board
decisions.detail: The petition asks the City to discontinue (give up) an abandoned portion of Cornwall Street. A public hearing will be scheduled when the Planning Board reports back. Councilor Flynn was out of the room.

decisions.title: Appointed John (Jack) Holzman to the Board of Adjustment
decisions.detail: Holzman fills a seat on the Zoning Board of Adjustment, the board that decides variance requests.

decisions.title: Approved the 2027 City Council meeting calendar
decisions.detail: The Council approved its meeting schedule for 2027.

decisions.title: Approved community events including First Night and Market Square Day
decisions.detail: Through the consent agenda (routine items approved in one vote), the Council approved the New Castle 10K, a Halloween costume paddle on October 25, First Night on December 31, 2026, Children's Day, the 50th Market Square Day Festival and 10K, and Summer in the Street in 2027.

decisions.title: Accepted a $500 Senior Activity Center luncheon donation and a granite bench for Four Tree Island
decisions.detail: Karen Parnes donated $500 to the luncheon fund, and the Council separately accepted a donated granite bench at Four Tree Island.

discussed.title: Parking ecosystem report
discussed.detail: Deputy City Manager Carl Weber reported on downtown workforce parking, RAPP, Parrott Avenue and its lot, ParkMobile fees and free parking locations.

discussed.title: High Hanover garage rate item not taken up
discussed.detail: Councilor Bagley's item on keeping the High Hanover garage rate at or below on-street rates was not taken up.

discussed.title: CIP citizen request subcommittee
discussed.detail: The Mayor named Councilors Tabor, Blalock and Moreau to the subcommittee that reviews resident Capital Improvement Plan requests.

discussed.title: City Manager updates
discussed.detail: The airport air traffic control tower is back in operation. A public input meeting on the Mechanic Street Pump Station feasibility study is set for September 21 at 6:20 p.m. in City Hall Conference Room A.

public_comment.gist: Speakers raised the Fleet Street bike lane and parking (one in support of the contraflow lane), automated license plate reader (FLOCK) cameras, and raising nonresident on-street rates along with a shuttle loop.
Matt Flynn spoke in support. Arthur Carakatsane raised pedestrian access for Portwalk residents. Tyler Garzo supported the plan and asked about a wider lane.

coming_up.item: First Night Portsmouth 2027
Shuttle Loop and Public Transit Working Group report due to the Council
Children's Day
50th Annual Market Square Day Festival and 10K Road Race
Summer in the Street begins (also July 10, 17, 24, 31 and August 7)

council_meetings.headline: A proposal to raise downtown on-street and lot parking to $3 an hour (then $6) failed 3-5 on a roll call, and the Council agreed to reconsider it on September 14.

decisions.title: Rejected raising downtown parking to $3 an hour for 3 hours, then $6 an hour
decisions.detail: The proposal would have set FY2027 on-street and lot parking rates. After 12 public speakers, many focused on downtown workers, councilors discussed signage, workforce parking, street versus garage pricing and timing. Several, including the Mayor, said they needed more time and a better plan for workforce parking and for parking revenue.

decisions.title: Agreed to reconsider the parking rate vote on September 14
decisions.detail: Assistant Mayor Kelley asked for data from the parking work session to help with reconsideration. The City Manager suggested a report back on September 14.

decisions.title: Passed first reading to move Fleet Street parking to the east side and make the street one-way
decisions.detail: Two unanimous votes: one moves parking spaces from the west to the east side of Fleet Street, and one makes Fleet Street one-way from Congress Street to Hanover Street. Councilors discussed effects on outdoor dining, wider sidewalks and a contraflow bike lane (a bike lane running against car traffic). Hearings and second reading are set for September 14.

decisions.title: Adopted the annual traffic and parking omnibus ordinance
decisions.detail: The ordinance makes permanent changes to 15-minute parking, no-parking areas and limited-hours loading zones. No one spoke at the hearing. The Council passed second reading, suspended its rules and passed third and final reading. Assistant Mayor Kelley was out of the room for the final votes.

decisions.title: Adopted the new City building code
decisions.detail: The Council replaced Chapter 12 (Building Code) so it lines up with the state building code. Assistant Mayor Kelley was absent for the vote.

decisions.title: Passed first reading of zoning changes on variance procedures and when approvals expire
decisions.detail: The amendments touch procedures for variances (permission to break a zoning rule for one property), special exceptions and appeals, and the rules for when land use approvals expire or can be extended. Public hearing and second reading are set for September 14.

decisions.title: Asked the City Attorney to draft a license plate reader ordinance
decisions.detail: The City Attorney will review proposed ordinance language on automated license plate reader systems and return a final draft for first reading. She said state law strictly limits these devices to law enforcement and the Police Commission wants to weigh in.

decisions.title: Set polling hours for the September 8 primary and November 3 general election
decisions.detail: Polls will be open 8:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. for both the NH State Primary on September 8, 2026 and the NH General Election on November 3, 2026.

decisions.title: Approved tentative contracts with custodial supervisors and AFSCME 1386A
decisions.detail: Two separate unanimous votes approved tentative labor agreements with the custodial supervisors and with the AFSCME 1386A union.

decisions.title: Accepted a $10,000 donation for a memorial bench in Bohenko Gateway Park
decisions.detail: Bob Thoresen donated $10,000 toward a sculptural memorial bench honoring Sue Werner Thoresen, and the Council agreed to accept further private gifts for it. A second vote lets the Public Art Trust cover any remaining design, fabrication and installation costs, including a contract with Sijia Chen.

decisions.title: Scheduled a rolling stock work session for October 26
decisions.detail: The work session on City vehicles and equipment (rolling stock) is set for 6:00 p.m. on October 26, 2026. Councilor Hopkins wants to discuss biofuels.

decisions.title: Endorsed NHMA's 2027-2028 legislative policies
decisions.detail: On the Legislative Subcommittee's recommendation, the Council approved the NH Municipal Association's proposed legislative policies and principles for 2027-2028.

decisions.title: Rescinded the old license fee policy for encumbrances of City property
decisions.detail: Policy No. 2018-02, which set a license fee for using City property, was rescinded. Fees are now set through the Administrative Code fee process.

decisions.title: Scheduled first reading on board appointment and removal rules
decisions.detail: First reading of a change to Administrative Code Section 1.302 (D), covering appointments, terms and removal for City boards, is set for September 14.

decisions.title: Approved Turkey Trot race and Lieutenant Dan Band event
decisions.detail: Both event requests were approved on the consent agenda (routine items approved in one vote).

decisions.title: Appointed Wendi Alip to the Sustainability Committee
decisions.detail: The appointment of John (Jack) Holzman to the Zoning Board of Adjustment was listed for consideration at a later meeting.

discussed.title: Capital Improvement Plan kickoff
discussed.detail: Deputy City Manager Nathan Lunney presented the start of the capital planning process. Councilors encouraged residents to submit requests through the online portal.

discussed.title: Encumbrance permits report
discussed.detail: The City Manager gave a verbal report back on encumbrance permits.

public_comment.gist: Speakers, including several business owners and downtown workers, asked for affordable workforce parking, discounted worker rates, longer garage limits, park and ride options, use of private lots after hours, and putting parking revenue toward alternatives like transit.
Buzz Sherr asked the Council to wait for the legislature and let the Police Commission meet on license plate readers (FLOCK).
Sue Sterry asked whether the resident rate would change and whether a study had been done.

coming_up.item: Rolling stock (City vehicles and equipment) work session at 6:00 p.m.
NH General Election, polls open 8:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m.

council_meetings.headline: The Council approved about $21 million in borrowing for school, City, water and sewer projects, postponed the $600,000 fire apparatus bond to October 13, and continued its hearing on raising downtown parking rates.

decisions.title: Approved up to $6,500,000 in borrowing for school projects
decisions.detail: Resolution #13-2026 covers school facility improvements, elementary school upgrades, elementary playground upgrades, and school paving and roofing. Little Harbor School's playground is under construction and New Franklin School is next. Bonds need a two-thirds vote, which was met.
decisions.outcome: passed unanimously on a roll call vote

decisions.title: Approved up to $6,485,000 in borrowing for City projects, including police station and City Hall design
decisions.detail: Resolution #14-2026 covers ambulance replacement, building repairs, the Hampton Branch Rail Trail, storm drains, The Creek neighborhood reconstruction, Vaughan Mall restoration, and design of the police facility and municipal complex. Several councilors spoke in support of the municipal building project.
decisions.outcome: passed unanimously on a roll call vote

decisions.title: Postponed the $600,000 fire apparatus bond to October 13
decisions.detail: Resolution #15-2026 would borrow up to $600,000 for one fire apparatus. Discussion centered on the fire boat: Councilor Blalock opposed the cost, while Councilors Bagley and Cook supported buying a boat. Four residents spoke, mostly about cost. The Council tabled (set aside) the item to October 13.

decisions.title: Approved up to $4,900,000 in borrowing for water projects
decisions.detail: Resolution #16-2026 covers water line replacement, well station improvements, Madbury Water Treatment Plant repairs, treatment at the Portsmouth and Collins wells, The Creek neighborhood and Vaughan Mall. It may use the State Revolving Fund loan program.
decisions.outcome: passed unanimously on a roll call vote

decisions.title: Approved up to $3,100,000 in borrowing for sewer and drainage projects
decisions.detail: Resolution #17-2026 covers wastewater pumping stations, the Peirce Island Wastewater Treatment Facility, storm drainage and Vaughan Mall.
decisions.outcome: passed unanimously on a roll call vote

decisions.title: Amended the proposed downtown parking rates to $3 and $6 an hour, then continued the hearing
decisions.detail: The amended motion would set FY2027 on-street and lot parking at $3 an hour for the first 3 hours and $6 an hour after that, with no change to resident rates. Councilors said the public is confused by several parking changes at once, and two speakers asked that revenue go to transportation alternatives. The hearing was continued, so no final rate vote was taken.

decisions.title: Scheduled an August 17 work session on parking rates and how revenue is used
decisions.detail: The work session at 6:00 pm on August 17 will cover higher on-street parking rates and uses of the money. Councilors raised ideas such as a downtown shuttle loop, electronic garage space signs, and involving COAST (the regional bus service).

decisions.title: Accepted the Vaughan Mall redesign plan
decisions.detail: The plan was accepted substantially as presented. It does not rule out later carrying out the 2017 plans for Vaughan Mall, the Worth Lot and the Bridge Street Lot. The City Manager said there will be a net loss of trees, with new greenery and trees planted.

decisions.title: Supported the concept of a donated "City of the Open Door" art piece for Vaughan Mall
decisions.detail: The Public Art Review Committee recommended the concept, which came from the LGBTQ+ community. The group wanted permission before fundraising; there is no request for proposals or timeline yet. Councilor Bagley objected to another group fundraising at the same time as a Sister City gift.

decisions.title: Released remaining public access TV trust funds to PPMtv
decisions.detail: The City Manager will direct the Trustees of the Trust Funds to release the remaining money in the Cable Television Public Access Charitable Trust to Portsmouth Public Media Television, Inc. Staff said no more money is likely to come into the trust.

decisions.title: Accepted a $776,653 state opioid abatement grant for social workers and housing help
decisions.detail: The two-year grant from the NH Department of Health and Human Services pays for an additional Police Department social worker, an additional School Department social worker, and housing funds for the Welfare Department.

decisions.title: Accepted a $24,100 state highway safety grant
decisions.detail: The grant supports six highway safety initiatives run through the Police Commission.

decisions.title: Accepted a $4,500 Elks donation for lifeguard training at the indoor pool
decisions.detail: Portsmouth Lodge of Elks No. 97 donated $4,500 to cover American Red Cross lifeguard training fees for the Portsmouth Indoor Pool.

decisions.title: Accepted a historic marker for Stoodley's Tavern on Hancock Street
decisions.detail: The Ranger Chapter Daughters of the American Revolution will donate a marker noting that Paul Revere alerted local Patriots there on December 12, 1775, before they seized gunpowder and cannon from Fort William and Mary. Public Works will recommend the exact spot.

decisions.title: Sent the draft Housing Action Plan to the Planning Board and set public input sessions
decisions.detail: The Planning Board will review it on August 20, 2026. Public information and input sessions are set for September 23 in the Levenson Room at the Portsmouth Public Library and September 28 as part of the City Council meeting.

decisions.title: Gave final approval to moving public property license fees out of ordinance
decisions.detail: This housekeeping change to Chapter 6 means fees for using public property will be adopted through the Administrative Code fee process. The Council passed second reading, suspended its rules and passed third and final reading the same night.

decisions.title: Passed second reading of the new City building code
decisions.detail: The replacement Chapter 12 lines up with the state building code. It must go to the state Building Code Review Board before third and final reading, set for August 17. Councilor Cook said she would like a green building code developed later.

decisions.title: Passed first reading of the annual traffic and parking omnibus ordinance
decisions.detail: The changes cover 15-minute parking, no-parking areas and limited-hours loading zones. A public hearing and second reading are set for August 17, with a presentation on the locations.

decisions.title: Sent a letter about 0 Elm Street to Legal and the Planning Board
decisions.detail: The letter from Attorney Colby T. Gamester was referred for a report back.

decisions.title: Approved three running and cycling events
decisions.detail: Through the consent agenda (routine items approved in one vote), the Council approved the Granite State Wheeler's annual Seacoast Country bicycle ride, the St. Paddy's 5k/10k and the Eastern States 20 Miler and Half Marathon.

decisions.title: Accepted Paul Mannle's resignation from the Zoning Board of Adjustment
decisions.detail: The resignation took effect July 1, 2026, and the City will send a letter of thanks.

discussed.title: Coakley Landfill update
discussed.detail: Planning Director Peter Britz gave an overview of the Coakley Landfill site and its status. Coakley Landfill Group meetings are open to the public with time for comment.

discussed.title: Technology working group proposed
discussed.detail: The Mayor proposed a citizen working group on using technology to improve City services, with a report by January 2027. The item was moved to August 17.

discussed.title: City Manager updates
discussed.detail: Brief verbal updates on DPW project web pages and the online guide for residents going before land use boards.

public_comment.gist: Speakers raised problems with the RAPP parking program for hospitality workers (citing a petition with 2,000 signatures), regional housing issues, public comment at work sessions, a DAR plaque at Stoodley's Tavern, hiding personal contact details in published emails, and splitting the police and municipal building projects.

public_comment.topic: School and City project bond hearings
public_comment.gist: Tyler Garza asked that school paving and roofing be listed separately. On the City projects bond, Susan Sterry described positive public feedback on the municipal building project, Petra Huda asked for transparency on each bond sale, and Esther Kennedy questioned costs and the need for another ambulance.
Esther Kennedy, Erik Anderson, Sue Sterry and Petra Huda spoke about the fire boat, including its cost, who outside Portsmouth should help pay, and security on the water.
Tyler Garzo and Colin Scholler supported higher rates but said parking money should go to transportation alternatives.

council_meetings.headline: The Council adopted a policy that Community Power should not re-enroll customers when its rates are 5% or more above Eversource's, and accepted about $4.6 million in state PFAS settlement money for drinking water treatment.

decisions.title: Set a policy to skip Community Power re-enrollment when its rates are 5% or more above Eversource
decisions.detail: Community Power (CPCNH) buys electricity in bulk for residents. A "customer refresh" re-enrolls customers who are not in the program. Under this policy, CPCNH would not do a refresh if its rates are 5% or more higher than Eversource's. The Energy Advisory Committee had recommended no action, noting a pause could create two tiers of customers.
decisions.outcome: passed 6-1 on a roll call vote

decisions.title: Amended the Community Power motion to use a 5% threshold
decisions.detail: The original motion would have stopped a refresh whenever CPCNH rates were higher than Eversource's at all. This amendment set the trigger at 5% or more.
decisions.outcome: passed 4-3 on a roll call vote

decisions.title: Rejected a 10% threshold for pausing Community Power re-enrollment
decisions.detail: An earlier amendment would have withheld a refresh only when CPCNH rates were 10% higher than Eversource's.
decisions.outcome: failed 1-6 on a roll call vote

decisions.title: Accepted $3,062,540 in state PFAS settlement money for Portsmouth Water Works
decisions.detail: PFAS are long-lasting "forever chemicals" found in some water supplies. The NH Department of Environmental Services allocated this settlement money to the City for drinking water treatment on the Portsmouth Water Works system.

decisions.title: Accepted $1,563,527 in state PFAS settlement money for the Pease Tradeport water system
decisions.detail: This is a separate NHDES allocation for PFAS drinking water treatment on the Pease Tradeport system.

decisions.title: Gave final approval to moving on-street parking fees into the fee committee process
decisions.detail: No one spoke at the public hearing. The Council passed second reading, then suspended its rules and passed third and final reading. It also scheduled a public hearing on August 3 to enact the fees staff recommended.

decisions.title: Scheduled public hearings on $21.6 million in borrowing for FY27 projects
decisions.detail: Proposed bonds (City borrowing) are $6,500,000 for school projects, $6,485,000 for various City projects, $600,000 for fire apparatus, $4,900,000 for water projects and $3,100,000 for sewer projects. Hearings and adoption votes are set for August 3.

decisions.title: Scheduled first reading to make Fleet Street one-way with a contraflow bike lane
decisions.detail: Following the Parking and Traffic Safety Committee's recommendation, the change would make Fleet Street one-way from Congress Street to Hanover Street, keep on-street parking, and add a bike lane running against traffic. First reading is set for August 3.

decisions.title: Passed first reading of a new City building code to match state code
decisions.detail: The ordinance replaces Chapter 12 to line up with the state building code. Councilor Cook asked why the local green building section (1208) was removed; staff said anything that differs from state code needs state approval and the green building rules may be placed elsewhere later. Public hearing and second reading are set for August 3.

decisions.title: Passed first reading on moving public property license fees out of ordinance
decisions.detail: The change adds Section 6.111 on fees to Chapter 6 (permits and licenses for using public property). Public hearing and second reading are set for August 3.

decisions.title: Scheduled first reading of the annual traffic and parking omnibus ordinance
decisions.detail: Each year the City makes permanent the temporary parking and traffic rules approved over the past 12 months. This year's changes cover 15-minute parking, no-parking areas and loading zones. First reading is set for August 3.

decisions.title: Granted a drain line license under the Parrott Avenue lot for 134 Pleasant Street
decisions.detail: Double MC LLC may build and maintain drainage under the City's Parrott Avenue parking lot for its approved project at 134 Pleasant Street. The Planning Board recommended the owner be required to repair or move the drain at its own expense.

decisions.title: Appointed Gary Dozier to the Police Commission
decisions.detail: Dozier will serve from August 1, 2026 until the next municipal election in November 2027.

decisions.title: Adopted five Child Care Task Force recommendations
decisions.detail: The recommendations are free pre-inspections, a plain language zoning guide, parking standards suited to childcare, naming childcare in the FY28 Community Development Block Grant process, and welcoming the new state laws.

decisions.title: Asked the Planning Board to study creating a Heritage Commission
decisions.detail: A Heritage Commission could add review for historic buildings, help preserve older homes that are naturally affordable, apply for grants and educate the public. The Planning Board is to report back by September 28, 2026.

decisions.title: Re-established the Veteran Organization committee
decisions.detail: The group would help local veterans with resources and fundraising. Applications will open to the community.

decisions.title: Asked for plain-language one-page guides to land use boards and permits
decisions.detail: The City Manager will work with planning, inspection and land use board chairs on simple guides for people going before a board or seeking a permit for the first time, with a report back August 3.

decisions.title: Requested report backs on sidewalk encumbrance permits, Vaughan Mall design and rolling stock
decisions.detail: Three separate unanimous votes ask staff to report on long-term sidewalk blockages from construction permits, on the Vaughan Mall design before August 3, and on how vehicles and equipment (rolling stock) fit into the capital plan.

decisions.title: Accepted a $500 donation to the Senior Activity Center luncheon fund
decisions.detail: The donation came from resident and Senior Activity Center member Karen Parnes.

discussed.title: SchoolCare lawsuit
discussed.detail: The City Attorney said the City sued SchoolCare to challenge a $1.57 million assessment. The court ordered SchoolCare to keep paying school claims during the case and paused the City's suit while a similar Dover lawsuit proceeds.

discussed.title: Banfield Road lawsuit dismissed
discussed.detail: The owner of 375 Banfield Road had sued the City claiming it dumped toxic material there in the late 1960s, which the City denied. The plaintiff agreed to dismiss all claims with no damages paid. The City Attorney said this is not connected to the owners' rezoning request.

discussed.title: Fleet Street reconstruction report
discussed.detail: Traffic Engineer Eric Eby presented the Fleet Street Section 1 plan. Councilors asked about a loading zone, tree cover and traffic flow on Congress Street.

discussed.title: Housing Action Plan draft
discussed.detail: The Housing Committee finished a working draft of the Housing Action Plan, now posted on the City website.

discussed.title: Arts and cultural banner pilot
discussed.detail: Staff proposed a pilot City banner program. Applications would be accepted January 1 to February 15, banners would run April to June and July to September, and a report back would come at the end of 2027.

discussed.title: Complete Streets policy and Sister Cities fund
discussed.detail: The City Manager said the City has followed its Complete Streets design guidelines for nine years and will continue. A new special revenue fund was set up for Sister Cities, with Mary Carey Foley as first donor in honor of Eileen Foley.

discussed.title: Zoning Board vacancy
discussed.detail: Paul Mannle resigned from the Zoning Board of Adjustment effective July 1, 2026. The Mayor held the appointment of Jack Holzman to that board until the next meeting.

public_comment.gist: Speakers asked for earlier posting of meeting notices and materials (citing the Mechanic Street Pump Station presentation), raised a misplaced stop sign at Hodgdon Way and Gate Street, asked about the fire apparatus bond, and asked how many Complete Streets determinations have come to the Council since 2013.

council_meetings.headline: Councilors on the Municipal Building Blue Ribbon Committee presented a phased plan to renovate the police station and City Hall, and the Council scheduled a work session on it before July 13.

decisions.title: Scheduled a work session on the police station and City Hall renovation plan
decisions.detail: The Municipal Building Blue Ribbon Committee described a nine-phase plan. Councilor Bagley said phases 1 to 5 (police station) are estimated at $42,215,000 and phases 6 to 9 (rest of City Hall) at $58,634,000. The Council will hold a work session (a discussion meeting with no votes) before the July 13 meeting.

decisions.title: Approved the Deputy Police Chief's employment agreement
decisions.detail: The Council approved the employment agreement for Deputy Chief of Police Maloney. Councilor Blalock spoke in support.

decisions.title: Passed first reading on moving on-street parking fees to the fee committee process
decisions.detail: The change to the parking meter rates ordinance means on-street parking fees will be set through the Fee Study Committee process instead of written into the ordinance. A public hearing and second reading are set for July 13.

decisions.title: Scheduled first reading on moving public property license fees out of ordinance
decisions.detail: A housekeeping change to Chapter 6 would add a new fees section so fees for using public property are approved through the Fee Study Committee. First reading is set for July 13.

decisions.title: Extended the Players Ring lease by one year
decisions.detail: The City Manager may negotiate and sign Lease Amendment 5 with the Players Ring theater. Councilors Blalock and Cook praised the group as tenants and for its service to the community.

decisions.title: Updated the City's street vending policy
decisions.detail: The amendments to Policy 2009-04 identify three vending sites: Market Square where the holiday tree goes up, outside the Hanover Street parking garage, and Vaughan Mall. Applications are being accepted.

decisions.title: Released remaining payments for the Nebi sculpture contract
decisions.detail: The Trustees of the Trust Funds will pay out the remaining phases of the contract, $30,000, $20,000 and $7,500, as the City Manager directs.

decisions.title: Released $3,000 to repair the "Cod and the Mortal Sea" sculpture
decisions.detail: Money from the Public Art Trust Fund will pay for repairs and reinforcement of the sculpture in Bohenko Park.

decisions.title: Asked planners to look at pre-approved ADU plans from other communities
decisions.detail: An ADU (accessory dwelling unit) is a small second home on a lot, like a backyard cottage. Planning & Sustainability, with the Housing Committee and Planning Board, will review pre-approved ADU designs used elsewhere to see if Portsmouth can adopt any. Councilor Tabor asked how such plans would fit historic district guidelines.

decisions.title: Approved a Community Power communication plan
decisions.detail: The Energy Advisory Committee's plan aims to make residents more aware of electric rate options. Councilor Tabor stressed that residents can opt out and choose Eversource at any time. Councilors discussed postcards, mailers, the website, email and Channel 22 as ways to notify people.

decisions.title: Extended the outside auditor contract with CliftonLarsonAllen for three years
decisions.detail: On the Audit Committee's recommendation, the City Manager may sign a three-year extension with the firm that performs the City's independent annual audit.

decisions.title: Sent a resident letter on a Complete Streets policy to the City Manager
decisions.detail: Tyler Garzo's letter about a Complete Streets policy (street design for walking, biking and transit as well as cars) was referred to the City Manager for a report back.

decisions.title: Approved Pure Barre community event and the 31st Halloween Parade
decisions.detail: Both event requests were approved on the consent agenda (routine items approved in one vote).

decisions.title: Made appointments to the Cemetery Committee and Cable and Broadband Internet Commission
decisions.detail: Karyn DeNicola joins the Cemetery Committee. Jim Wilson moves from alternate to regular member, and Ash Chicooree and Jeff Abrams were reappointed, on the Cable and Broadband Internet Commission.

discussed.title: Police Commission vacancy
discussed.detail: Gary Dozier was put forward for consideration to fill the Police Commission seat of Jay Lieberman, who plans to resign July 31, 2026, until the November 2027 municipal election. He was the next highest vote-getter. No vote was taken at this meeting.

discussed.title: City Manager Evaluation Committee
discussed.detail: Councilors Cook, Tabor and Moreau will form this year's committee to evaluate the City Manager.

discussed.title: Capital Improvement Plan requests due September 18
discussed.detail: The City Manager said the deadline for resident and board requests for the FY28-32 Capital Improvement Plan (the City's long-range list of building and equipment projects) is September 18, 2026.

discussed.title: Pease Development Authority update
discussed.detail: The City Manager recapped the June 16 board meeting, including a planned temporary 45-day shutdown of the air traffic control tower at Portsmouth International Airport and the first American Cruise Lines arrival.

discussed.title: Artist studio study confirmed eligible for housing trust funds
discussed.detail: The Trustees of Trust Funds confirmed the Artist Live Work Studio Study can use Below Market Rate Housing Trust Fund money.

public_comment.gist: Dee Forte said the Cemetery Committee will mark Revolutionary War soldier graves with signs and an online map. Other speakers raised audit oversight, meeting minutes, the cost of the sculpture repair, teacher wages, the Deputy Police Chief's appointment, and a request for a Council response to a letter.

coming_up.item: Audit Committee meeting at 4 pm

council_meetings.headline: The Council adopted the FY27 city budget (General Fund passed 8-1) and gave final approval to the Resident Access Parking Program (RAPP) pilot 8-1.

decisions.title: Adopted the FY27 General Fund budget
decisions.detail: Resolution #8-2026 sets spending for the City's general operating departments and services for the year ending June 30, 2027, as amended during the meeting. During the budget discussion, Councilor Cook said the budget could not be supported without money for the Artist Live/Work Studio Study included.
decisions.outcome: passed 8-1 on a roll call vote

decisions.title: Rejected adding a $56,000 fuel subsidy to the budget
decisions.detail: Councilor Bagley proposed adding $56,000 to the FY27 budget because fuel costs rose after the budget was prepared. Mayor McEachern and Councilor Blalock spoke against it.
decisions.review_note: The recorded motion combines suspending the rules with the $56,000 amendment, and the discussion is written after the roll call. Confirm the 1-8 roll call was on the amendment itself.

decisions.title: Kept the Fire Department's Deputy Chief of Training position in the budget
decisions.detail: Mayor McEachern proposed cutting $174,740, the cost of the Deputy Chief for Training position, from the Fire Department budget. Fire Chief McQuillen explained the reasons for the position, and Councilor Hopkins described the value of hands-on training.
decisions.review_note: OCR text around the seconder is garbled ("Seconded by Councilor ... Blalock and voted.)"). Confirm the seconder against the PDF.

decisions.title: Directed staff to seek a federal grant for a replacement fire boat
decisions.detail: Instead of cutting the fire boat line in the capital plan from $900,000 to $150,000, the Mayor revised his motion. The City Manager and Fire Chief will ask the U.S. Coast Guard for a letter of support for a FEMA Port Security Grant application, work with the state's Congressional delegation, and report back before any borrowing is requested.

decisions.title: Cut $50,000 for a city fleet electrification plan from the budget
decisions.detail: The Council removed $50,000 in capital spending for a plan to electrify the City vehicle fleet. Councilor Cook noted there are no federal funds for this, and Councilor Bagley said a study is not needed for equipment that does not yet exist.

decisions.title: Funded a $65,000 Artist Live/Work Studio Study from the below-market housing trust
decisions.detail: The Trustees of the Trust Funds may spend $65,000 from the Below Market Rate Housing Trust Fund on a study of artist live/work studios as below-market housing. Councilor Tabor said that fund is meant to help people afford housing and opposed using it this way.

decisions.title: Removed the $65,000 artist studio study from capital spending once trust funds are released
decisions.detail: A second motion cuts $65,000 from the FY27 capital budget for the same study, once the Trustees release the money from the housing trust fund.

decisions.title: Raised nonresident fees at Spinnaker Point
decisions.detail: New nonresident rates: $575 a year or $50 a month for adults, $300 a year or $35 a month for seniors, and a $25 daily guest fee.

decisions.title: Adopted the FY27 municipal fee schedule
decisions.detail: Resolution #7-2026 sets City fees for the year, as amended. Councilors discussed dock utility fees, which are a flat rate with no resident discount.
decisions.outcome: passed unanimously on a roll call vote

decisions.title: Adopted the FY27 Water Fund budget
decisions.detail: Resolution #9-2026 sets spending for running the City water system for the year ending June 30, 2027.
decisions.outcome: passed unanimously on a roll call vote

decisions.title: Adopted the FY27 Sewer Fund budget
decisions.detail: Resolution #10-2026 sets spending for running the City sewer system for the year ending June 30, 2027.
decisions.outcome: passed unanimously on a roll call vote

decisions.title: Adopted FY27 spending from special revenues, the housing endowment trust and committed fund balance
decisions.detail: Resolution #11-2026 approves spending from special revenue accounts, the Portsmouth Housing Endowment Trust and committed fund balance (money already set aside for set purposes).
decisions.outcome: passed unanimously on a roll call vote

decisions.title: Approved the City's FY27 investment policy
decisions.detail: Resolution #12-2026 approves the rules for how the City invests its money for the coming fiscal year.
decisions.outcome: passed unanimously on a roll call vote

decisions.title: Gave final approval to the RAPP parking pilot rates
decisions.detail: The ordinance sets parking rates for the one-year Resident Access Parking Program pilot, which gives residents priority for on-street parking. Councilor Blalock said he did not think it would meet its goals; the Mayor and Councilors Bagley and Cook spoke in support.
decisions.outcome: passed 8-1 on a roll call vote

decisions.title: Adopted the RAPP pilot policy
decisions.detail: The Council adopted City Council Policy No. 2026-01, which sets out how the Resident Access Parking Program pilot will run.

decisions.title: Started changing how on-street parking fees are set
decisions.detail: After a staff report on on-street and lot parking fees, the Council set first reading for June 22 on a Chapter 7 change so on-street fees are set the same way as other fees, through the Administrative Code with recommendations from the Fee Schedule Study Committee.

decisions.title: Adopted updated fire codes
decisions.detail: The Council passed second reading of the fire code amendment (Chapter 5, Article IX), then suspended its rules and passed third and final reading the same night.

decisions.title: Supported state bill HB 1491 on municipal risk pools
decisions.detail: At the NH Municipal Association's request, the Council passed a resolution urging the Governor to sign HB 1491, which allows non-assessment risk pools (shared insurance programs for towns).

decisions.title: Asked staff for a refined revenue model and a vacancy budgeting approach before October 15
decisions.detail: Two separate unanimous votes ask staff to report back before October 15, 2026, in time to set the tax rate, on a refined revenue model and on a way to budget for job vacancies.

decisions.title: Accepted a $380,178 federal grant for the NH Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force
decisions.detail: The grant comes from the U.S. Department of Justice's Office of Juvenile Justice and Delinquency Prevention.

decisions.title: Accepted an illuminated poem installation from Friendship City Santarcangelo, Italy
decisions.detail: The gift is an illuminated script artwork by artist Tiziano Corbelli showing the poem "The Air" by Tonino Guerra in English and Italian. It will be installed in Vaughan Mall for about a year as part of the Vaughan Mall project.

decisions.title: Awarded a $10,000 public art grant for a high school mural project
decisions.detail: The grant from the PNH400th Anniversary Education and Public Art Trust goes to "History Through Art Mural Making," submitted by Terrence Parker with the Portsmouth High School Art Program.

decisions.title: Accepted a donated bike rack for the Atlantic Heights bus stop
decisions.detail: The Atlantic Heights Neighborhood donated a bike rack, which Public Works will place at the Atlantic Heights bus stop.

decisions.title: Sent a petition about AI data centers to the Legal Department
decisions.detail: The Legal Department will review the petition and report back.

decisions.title: Sent a 361 Hanover Street license request to the Planning Board
decisions.detail: Property owners asked for a landscaping license and pole license over City property. The Planning Board will make a recommendation. Councilor Moreau recused himself (stepped out of the vote).

decisions.title: Asked staff to report back on making Fleet Street one-way between Congress and Hanover
decisions.detail: The Parking & Traffic Safety Committee item on one-way traffic and on-street parking on that block was pulled out for separate review, and staff will report back on its recommendation.

decisions.title: Renewed The 100 Club's valet license
decisions.detail: Councilor Bagley recused himself.

decisions.title: Approved Irreverent Warriors hike on August 29 and a Pilates series in Prescott Park
decisions.detail: Through the consent agenda (routine items approved in one vote), the Council approved the Irreverent Warriors New Hampshire "Portsmouth Silkies Hike" on August 29, 2026 and a FORM Fitness Pilates series in Prescott Park.

decisions.title: Made reappointments to the Cemetery Committee, Conservation Commission and others
decisions.detail: Three people were reappointed to the Cemetery Committee and two to the Conservation Commission, and new members were named to the Arts and Cultural Commission and the Sustainability Committee.

discussed.title: Community Power presentation
discussed.detail: State Consumer Advocate Donald Kreis presented on the Community Power Coalition of New Hampshire (CPCNH), which buys electricity in bulk for towns. Councilors asked about outreach, how easy it is to opt in or out, an independent report, and a possible conflict of interest involving Calpine Corporation.

discussed.title: Open enrollment vote no longer needed
discussed.detail: The City Manager reported that the state open enrollment legislation failed this session, so the planned vote on the school district's policy was not needed.

discussed.title: School Food Insecurity Task Force
discussed.detail: Councilor Flynn said the task force's first meeting is set for June 10, 2026.

discussed.title: Community Power communication plan moved
discussed.detail: Councilor Tabor's item on a Community Power communication plan was moved to the June 22 agenda.

public_comment.gist: Speakers raised transparency of the Community Power refresh, how meeting minutes and videos are kept, a bike rack donation in Atlantic Heights, the level of detail in minutes, the City Clerk's role in elections, and the cost of living in Portsmouth.
Petra Huda, Rick Becksted, Erik Anderson, Paige Trace and Esther Kennedy spoke on budget data, possible savings, the fire boat, the Housing Trust Fund, inefficiencies, and employee-related increases.

council_meetings.headline: The Council passed second reading of the Resident Access Parking Program (RAPP) pilot rates 7-1 and held the first public hearing on the proposed FY27 city budget.

decisions.title: Passed second reading of the RAPP parking pilot rates
decisions.detail: RAPP is a one-year pilot that gives residents priority for on-street parking. Deputy City Manager Weber gave an update, and the Council heard a fee committee update and discussed ParkMobile fees. Third and final reading is set for June 8.

decisions.title: Continued the FY27 budget public hearing to June 8
decisions.detail: The Council held a public hearing on the proposed budget for July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027. Three residents spoke, and Councilors Bagley and Cook said they support the proposed budget. The hearing will continue on June 8.

decisions.title: Approved a "Good of the Hive" mural contract for the Middle School
decisions.detail: The City Manager may sign an agreement with Matthew Willey Murals Inc. for a mural at Portsmouth Middle School, to be installed in fall 2027. A separate unanimous vote lets the Trustees of Trust Funds pay the artist from the Public Arts Trust money tied to the Middle School addition's percent-for-art contribution, up to the amount in that fund.

decisions.title: Scheduled a vote on the school open enrollment policy for June 8
decisions.detail: After a public hearing where the School Board Chair described the board's approach and updates to state bill SB751 on funding, the Council set its vote on the Portsmouth School District open enrollment policy for June 8.

decisions.title: Passed first reading of updated fire codes
decisions.detail: The Council passed first reading of a change to the City's adopted fire codes and set a public hearing and second reading for June 8.

decisions.title: Approved revised South Meeting House lease and accepted a $70,634.90 repayment
decisions.detail: The City Manager may approve a revised lease of the South Meeting House with the Schleyer Foundation and a related sublease to PMAC. The City also accepted $70,634.90 from the Schleyer Foundation to repay Community Development Block Grant funds.

decisions.title: Accepted a $499,576 federal Community Development Block Grant
decisions.detail: The City will accept and spend a $499,576 Community Development Block Grant from the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development.

decisions.title: Scheduled a June 22 work session on the Mechanic Street Pump Station replacement
decisions.detail: The Council set a work session (a discussion meeting with no votes) on replacing the Mechanic Street Pump Station for June 22, 2026 at 6:00 p.m.

decisions.title: Renewed the International Drive water tank license with NHDOT
decisions.detail: The City Manager may sign a renewal of the license agreement with the NH Department of Transportation for the International Drive water tank.

decisions.title: Approved a license and landscape agreement for 175 Fleet Street
decisions.detail: The City Manager may sign the 175 Fleet Street license and landscape agreement.

decisions.title: Approved St. John's Masonic Lodge parade on June 28 and a utility pole license
decisions.detail: Through the consent agenda (routine items approved in one vote), the Council approved the lodge's annual parade on Sunday, June 28, 2026 and pole license request 63-0771.

decisions.title: Made appointments to the Bicycle and Pedestrian and Citywide Neighborhood committees
decisions.detail: Tyler Garzo and Ryan Harper were appointed to the Bicycle and Pedestrian Blue Ribbon Committee, and Ken Hale and Christian Berling to the Citywide Neighborhood Committee. Several other reappointments and appointments were listed for consideration at a later meeting.

decisions.title: Accepted a $500 donation to the Senior Activity Center luncheon fund
decisions.detail: The City accepted a $500 donation for the Senior Activity Center luncheon fund.

discussed.title: Budget questions for the May 28 work session
discussed.detail: Councilors asked about the fire boat and school hiring. Answers and report backs from earlier work sessions are expected at the May 28 budget work session.

discussed.title: City Manager updates
discussed.detail: Informational items covered Household Hazardous Waste Day, the RAPP pilot policy, and a Clean Water State Revolving Fund grant for emerging contaminants tied to the Coakley Landfill Group.

public_comment.gist: Speakers raised the PARC-Hive mural, 250th anniversary celebrations, and Route 1.
Esther Kennedy, Tyler Garzo and Erik Anderson spoke on salary increases, hiring, education, boats, parking revenues, the budget increase and the fire boat.
Esther Kennedy spoke at the hearing. The minutes do not summarize her comments.
Tyler Garzo spoke at the hearing. The minutes do not summarize his comments.

council_meetings.headline: The Council changed the proposed Resident Access Parking Program (RAPP) pilot so a fee committee will set the nonresident and downtown worker rates, and pushed the public hearing to May 18.

decisions.title: Amended the RAPP parking pilot ordinance so the fee committee sets nonresident and worker rates
decisions.detail: RAPP is a one-year pilot that gives residents priority for on-street parking, tests charging nonresidents, and adds downtown worker parking on Parrott Avenue. The amendment says the parking rate for nonresidents and for registered downtown workers will be set by the fee study committee. The Acting City Attorney said this was a material change, so the Council voted to re-notice the public hearing and redo second reading on May 18.

decisions.title: Asked the fee committee to report back on RAPP rates by June 22
decisions.detail: The Council requested a report from the fee committee on the RAPP pilot by June 22, 2026.

decisions.title: Approved sewer ordinance change allowing fixed service fees
decisions.detail: The change lets the City collect fixed service fees on top of sewer use charges, following recommendations from the March 2 water and sewer rate study work session. No one spoke at the public hearing. The Council passed second reading, then suspended its rules and passed third and final reading the same night.

decisions.title: Adopted a three-tier water and sewer rate structure for FY27
decisions.detail: The Council adopted the recommended three-tier rate structure for water and sewer service for the 2027 fiscal year. In a tiered structure, the price per unit changes as usage goes up.

decisions.title: Scheduled a public hearing on the school district's open enrollment policy
decisions.detail: The Superintendent and School Board Chair said the School Board passed a cautious policy in case the state requires open enrollment starting July 1, 2026, and that many questions remain. The Council set a public hearing on the policy for May 18.

decisions.title: Asked the City Manager to study on-street parking rates without raising costs for residents
decisions.detail: The City Manager will report back with an analysis of on-street parking rates and policies in light of the expected garage rate increase. Any recommended changes must not raise on-street parking costs for Portsmouth residents.

decisions.title: Created a School Food Insecurity Taskforce with the School Board
decisions.detail: City staff will work with the School Board and school staff to set up a taskforce on students who lack reliable access to food, as called for in the Council's 2026-2027 goals. Preliminary findings are due by the end of the calendar year.

decisions.title: Appointed members to the Behavioral Health and Bicycle & Pedestrian Blue Ribbon Committees
decisions.detail: Five people were appointed to the Behavioral Health Blue Ribbon Committee and eleven to the Bicycle & Pedestrian Blue Ribbon Committee.

decisions.title: Named a new private street off Sagamore Avenue "Spruce Street"
decisions.detail: The new private street starting at the former 550 Sagamore Avenue address will be called Spruce Street.

decisions.title: Scheduled first reading of updated fire codes for May 18
decisions.detail: The Council set first reading of a change to the City's adopted fire codes (Chapter 5, Article IX) for the May 18 meeting.

decisions.title: Approved summer events: Go Skate Day, Sail Portsmouth and a Lafayette250 program
decisions.detail: Through the consent agenda (routine items approved in one vote), the Council approved Go Skate Day on June 21, the Sail Portsmouth maritime event July 23 to 26, and a Lafayette Trail program on May 27.

decisions.title: Accepted a $4,204 state grant for Household Hazardous Waste Collection Day
decisions.detail: The City Manager may sign a grant agreement with the NH Department of Environmental Services to accept $4,204 for the household hazardous waste collection day.

decisions.title: Accepted a $2,000 wellness reward from Health Trust
decisions.detail: The City accepted a $2,000 wellness reward from Health Trust.

discussed.title: City Clerk appointment not taken up
discussed.detail: The Mayor brought forward an appointment of Sally Kellar as City Clerk. The Acting City Attorney said that under the City Charter the City Manager, not the Council, appoints the City Clerk, so the item was not taken up.

discussed.title: Seacoast Greenway rail trail presentation
discussed.detail: David Allen of the NH Seacoast Greenway Alliance presented on the rail trail. Councilor Cook asked about possible murals along the trail.

discussed.title: Arts and cultural banner policy
discussed.detail: Councilor Cook asked the Legal Department to report back on the status of the arts and cultural banner policy.

discussed.title: City Manager updates
discussed.detail: The City Manager shared the FY27 budget meeting schedule and noted that dog license late fees can be avoided by licensing dogs before June 1. The Acting City Attorney gave a verbal update on SchoolCare.

public_comment.gist: Four speakers addressed the City Clerk appointment or the former City Clerk.
Speakers promoted a burger night benefiting the SPCA and upcoming Mental Health Awareness events.
Individual speakers raised the RAPP parking fee increase, affordable housing, Teacher Appreciation Week and meeting minutes, and speeding drivers.
Rick Becksted, Brooks Stevens, Robin Husslage and Tyler Garzo spoke at the hearing. The minutes do not summarize what they said.

council_meetings.headline: The Council approved $6,000,000 and $6,500,000 in state revolving fund loans for Fleet Street reconstruction and Greenland Well PFAS treatment, and voted to work with the Prescott Park Arts Festival on a Festival-funded covered stage.

decisions.title: Approved $6,000,000 in state clean water loans for Fleet Street reconstruction
decisions.detail: Adopts a resolution to join the Clean Water State Revolving Fund (a state program of low-cost loans for water projects) for up to $6,000,000 for the Fleet Street Area Reconstruction Phase 2B project. No one spoke at the public hearing.

decisions.title: Approved $6,500,000 in state drinking water loans for Greenland Well PFAS treatment
decisions.detail: Adopts a resolution to join the Drinking Water State Revolving Fund for up to $6,500,000 to treat PFAS (long-lasting chemicals) at the Greenland Well. No one spoke at the public hearing.

decisions.title: Voted to work with the Prescott Park Arts Festival on a covered stage
decisions.detail: The City will collaborate with the Prescott Park Arts Festival to plan and start park infrastructure improvements, including a covered stage and related structures, paid for by the Festival. Councilors asked for chances for public input. Four people spoke afterward on this item.

decisions.title: Asked Public Works to add Prescott Park maintenance to the capital plan
decisions.detail: After a staff report on Phase 1A of the Prescott Park Master Plan, Councilor Cook first moved to pause the plan after Phase 1A to focus on basic park needs. On the City Attorney's suggestion, she changed the motion to ask Public Works to include Prescott Park infrastructure maintenance in the Capital Improvement Plan instead.

decisions.title: Released Jay Smith Park trust funds based on the public art committee's plan
decisions.detail: Accepts the Public Art Review Committee's report on plans for Jay Smith Park and sends it to the Trustees of Trust Funds so they can pay out money from the Jay Smith Park Trust.

decisions.title: Passed first reading of parking rates for the resident parking pilot
decisions.detail: Amends parking meter rates (Chapter 7, Section 7.102) to set rates for the Resident Access Parking Program (RAPP) Pilot. Councilors asked staff to report back on whether community partner volunteers could be included. Public hearing and second reading are set for May 4, 2026.

decisions.title: Rejected a citywide mailer on Community Power pricing
decisions.detail: Would have sent an Every Door Direct Mail postcard to all households comparing Community Power pricing with Eversource and explaining how to opt out. Councilor Bagley stressed rate transparency; other councilors cited mailing cost and doubts about how well a paper mailer works.

decisions.title: Accepted a $1,450,000 state grant for the Market Street and Russell Street intersection
decisions.detail: A New Hampshire Department of Transportation grant, using state and federal funding, for intersection improvements.

decisions.title: Accepted a $41,000 Victims of Crime Award grant
decisions.detail: Accepts the VOCA grant as presented.

decisions.title: Updated an emergency management grant for the Emergency Operations Center
decisions.detail: Amends a previously approved Emergency Management Performance Grant from the NH Department of Safety to change the federal funding year and performance period dates from August 31, 2024 to August 31, 2026.

decisions.title: Supported filing a friend-of-the-court brief in a SchoolCare lawsuit

council_meetings.headline: The newly elected City Council, School Board and Police Commission were sworn in, and Mayor Deaglan McEachern began his third term with an inaugural address.

discussed.title: Oaths of office
discussed.detail: The City Clerk swore in Police Commissioners Buzz Scherr and Jay Lieberman; School Board members Lisa Rapaport, Steve Adler, Nancy Novelline Clayburgh, Brian French and Jennifer Shump; Councilors Kate Cook, John Tabor, Rich Blalock, Andrew Bagley, Beth Moreau, Michelle Flynn and Annie Hopkins; Assistant Mayor JoAnna "Jo" Kelley; and Mayor Deaglan McEachern. Fire Commissioners Richard Gamester and Jennifer Mosher-Matthes could not attend.

discussed.title: Mayor's inaugural address
discussed.detail: The Mayor said the city had approved new housing faster than any other New Hampshire community, created the Seacoast's first dedicated Housing Trust, expanded senior and veteran tax relief, and invested in climate resilience. He said rising costs and responsibilities pushed down from higher levels of government are a challenge ahead.

discussed.title: Remarks from state and federal officials
discussed.detail: State Senator Perkins-Kwoka and Congressman Pappas spoke, and staff read remarks from Senators Hassan and Shaheen.

council_meetings.headline: The Council unanimously approved a police union agreement that shortens the officer pay scale from 18 steps to 7, and sent the resident parking pilot to the Parking & Traffic Safety Committee for review.

decisions.title: Approved a new pay agreement with the police patrol officers' union
decisions.detail: The Memorandum of Agreement with the Portsmouth Police Patrolman's Union compresses the salary schedule from 18 steps to 7, effective January 1, 2026, so officers reach the top of the existing pay range faster. Staff and Police Chief Newport said junior officers are leaving for other departments because Portsmouth is no longer competitive.

decisions.title: Sent the Resident Access Parking Program pilot to the Parking & Traffic Safety Committee
decisions.detail: The pilot would charge non-residents $1.00 an hour and give free parking in designated zones outside the metered downtown to registered Portsmouth residents and School, Recreation and Library employees. policy_items.title: Recommended the FY2027-FY2031 Capital Improvement Plan to the City Council
policy_items.detail: The Capital Improvement Plan is the city's 5-year list of planned building, road and equipment projects. The board first voted (all in favor) to add $3 million to FY27 as a bond line item for a new parking garage. It then voted to recommend the City Council adopt the plan as amended (all in favor, City Manager Conard abstaining). One member of the public, speaking for the Arts and Cultural Commission, asked that artist live/work studio space be funded through a separate request.

policy_items.title: Historic District boundary: two Austin Street lots
policy_items.detail: Voted (all in favor) to ask the Historic District Commission for a recommendation on whether 43 Austin Street and 53 Austin Street should be included in the Historic District.

policy_items.title: Recommended Gateway zoning map changes
policy_items.detail: On a referral from the Housing Committee, voted (all in favor) to recommend the City Council schedule a first reading on rezoning certain parcels to the Gateway district, as presented.

policy_items.title: Advised against changing house-to-multifamily conversion rules for now (Section 10.812)
policy_items.detail: Voted (all in favor) to recommend the City Council not amend the rule on converting existing houses into multifamily homes at this time, and to take it up during the Master Plan process.

policy_items.title: Recommended zoning amendments on mechanical units and solar
policy_items.detail: Voted (all in favor) to recommend the City Council hold first reading on both. Mechanical systems such as HVAC units would not count as structures or toward building coverage, and power generators would need to be at least 5 feet from any lot line. The solar change limits roof-mounted solar to the roof area of the structures on the lot.

policy_items.title: Recommended zoning amendments for accessory dwelling units (House Bill 577)
policy_items.detail: Voted (all in favor) to recommend the City Council hold first reading on changes to match the new state ADU law. The action sheet says the recommendation was amended so ADUs are not permitted in the CD4 and CD5 downtown districts. The board said it preferred to keep the 750 square foot size limit.
policy_items.review_note: The action sheet says 'as amended to not permit ADUs in CD4/CD5 districts' (seconded by K. Conard), while the minutes record the motion as 'as presented' (seconded by Mr. Samonas).

policy_items.title: Recommended parking zoning amendment (Senate Bill 284)
policy_items.detail: Voted (all in favor) to recommend the City Council hold first reading. Staff said the parking table was changed so that 500 square feet or less would need half a parking space and more than 500 square feet one space, consistent with the new state law.

board_meetings.headline: In a work session with no votes, the board talked through Historic District boundary changes, City Council requests on parking rules, Gateway rezoning and house conversions, and several draft zoning amendments.

policy_items.title: Historic District boundary revision
policy_items.detail: The board reviewed the Historic District Commission's suggested boundary changes, which aim to reduce the number of properties split by the district line. The Chair noted that the 9 Middle Rd parcel appeared not meant to be included. Board members said they were fine with the recommendation with one change. Members also discussed how affected owners are notified. No vote was taken.

policy_items.title: Moving parking requirements into the site plan regulations
policy_items.detail: Discussion of a City Council request to move parking rules out of the zoning ordinance and into the site plan regulations (the board's own rules for reviewing project layouts). Members said this could allow more flexibility, since the board can waive site plan rules by vote. Staff said the work had started. No vote was taken.

policy_items.title: Rezoning certain parcels to Gateway
policy_items.detail: Discussion of a City Council request to rezone certain parcels to the Gateway district (a mixed-use zone). Members asked about sewer and other infrastructure, wetland buffers and property tax effects. Most members favored adding one more lot shown on the map, while Vice-Chair Coviello wanted city staff to look at it first. No vote was taken.

policy_items.title: Converting large older houses into multifamily housing (Section 10.812)
policy_items.detail: Staff described a change that would let owners convert existing pre-1980 houses into multifamily homes with less lot area per unit, without enlarging the building. Members discussed the need for housing and neighborhood character. The Chair asked to see the idea sketched out further. No vote was taken.

policy_items.title: Draft zoning amendments: mechanical units, solar, parking (Senate Bill 284), accessory dwelling units (House Bill 577) and multifamily in commercial districts (House Bill 631)
policy_items.detail: The board worked through draft wording. Mechanical units: HVAC units would no longer count as structures, but power generators would need a 5-foot setback from lot lines, matching fire code. Solar: members discussed size limits and wording for roof-mounted and ground-mounted panels. Parking: a size threshold would change from 750 to 500 square feet. ADUs (accessory dwelling units, a small second home on a lot): members discussed the owner-occupancy rule and the 750 square foot cap. House Bill 631: staff was still reviewing it with the Legal Department. No votes were taken.

policy_items.title: Wetland conditional use permit rules
policy_items.detail: Members discussed whether people improving a wetland buffer should still need a permit, and whether some requests could go only to the Conservation Commission through an administrative permit. No vote was taken.
